clue.text: Military unit also involved in scheme

indicators.note: the word for also is wrapped up inside the word for scheme

explanation.surface: A regiment gets caught up in some plot as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' signals the container: the second word sits within the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small army subdivision commanded by a lieutenant, a unit of soldiers.

clue.text: Conflict between mail companies after 1945

definitions.meaning: a battle between postal firms
following the Second World War

explanation.surface: Rival delivery firms fought it out once the war was over.
explanation.definitionFit: Postwar describes the period following World War Two, which ended in 1945.

clue.text: Italian lover serves sweet sherry

definitions.meaning: the Italian word for a lover or sweetheart
a sweetened style of oloroso sherry

explanation.surface: A Latin lothario pours glasses of sweet sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Italian for a lover, and names a sweetened kind of sherry.

clue.text: Children not at school before May

parts.note: off, as in off school, absent
May is a spring month, standing for the season

explanation.surface: Kids are off school before the start of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: May is a month of spring in the northern hemisphere, so the season stands for it; 'before' keeps the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's children or descendants.

clue.text: Giving assent whilst half asleep

definitions.meaning: moving the head down to say yes
dozing, head drooping

explanation.surface: Someone agrees while drowsing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means agreeing with a dip of the head and dozing drowsily.

clue.text: Wrongly claimed to be therapeutic

indicators.note: the word claimed is set out wrongly, signalling its letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some remedy was falsely said to have healing powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' rearranges the letters of CLAIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical treatment is concerned with healing, so the adjective works as a looser synonym of curative.

clue.text: Exploit and soak a feeble fellow

explanation.surface: Take advantage of a weakling and drench him.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a timid, spineless man.

clue.text: Dean is longing to join the party

explanation.surface: A college dean is keen to attend the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to join the' links the pieces, DO then YEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean, like a doyen, is the senior member of a body.

clue.text: Hymn tune played hourly in church

indicators.note: the word for hourly is placed inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
horal is an old word meaning hourly

explanation.surface: Church bells chime a hymn every hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective for hourly is a rare word; CE (Church of England) is the usual crossword church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a stately hymn tune, as in Lutheran church music.

clue.text: Just the dance for cavalrymen!

definitions.meaning: a quadrille danced by sets of couples
mounted soldiers carrying lances

explanation.surface: A dance especially suited to mounted soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancers was a nineteenth-century square dance and also means soldiers armed with lances.

clue.text: Derided for having tucked in too heartily

definitions.meaning: to mock or jeer at someone
ate greedily, gobbled food down

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked for overeating at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to jeer at and, informally, to eat hungrily and fast.

clue.text: Stretched out to store the wine

definitions.meaning: reclined, as in ... on the sofa
to put bottles in a cellar to mature

explanation.surface: Someone reclines in order to keep the bottles safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to recline, and also to put wine in a cellar for maturing.

clue.text: Delighted cry when TV doctor gets work

parts.note: Doctor Who, the long-running BBC science-fiction series
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone yells with joy when a famous TV medic finds employment.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of a British TV series; OP (opus) is the usual crossword 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud excited shout of joy or triumph.

clue.text: Hint given on reinvesting annuities

indicators.note: putting the annuities in again in a fresh form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip offered about putting pension money back into the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reinvesting' rearranges the letters of ANNUITIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest something indirectly, which is what hinting means.

clue.text: Getting new plants established is encouraging

definitions.meaning: making cuttings grow roots
cheering on, as in supporting a team

explanation.surface: A gardener's cuttings taking hold is a hopeful sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is chiefly American: rooting for a side means cheering it on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both striking roots in soil and cheering for a team.

clue.text: Customers who push the boat out

definitions.meaning: clients, particularly gamblers at a bookmaker
people propelling a flat-bottomed boat with a pole

explanation.surface: Big-spending shoppers who splash out generously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'push the boat out' is a British idiom for spending lavishly, but here it is literal: on rivers like the Cam, punts are poled along.
explanation.definitionFit: Clients and gamblers are informally called this, as are people propelling a punt.

clue.text: Unsurpassed in French

parts.note: the French words meaning not equal, used in English for something peerless

explanation.surface: Someone is the best in a French class.
explanation.definitionFit: A word borrowed from French meaning having no equal, hence matchless.

clue.text: Reel around in shock

definitions.meaning: to walk unsteadily, lurching
to astonish greatly

explanation.surface: Someone staggers about in a state of shock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to totter unsteadily and also to astonish or amaze.

clue.text: Test car components, then disperse

indicators.note: the test car's parts are broken into components, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Check the parts of a car, then spread them about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'components' rearranges TESTCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter is to spread widely, the same as to disperse.

clue.text: In the morning everyone meets up back at The Flask

indicators.note: the words for everyone and up are read backwards

explanation.surface: Early in the day, the whole crowd gathers again at a pub called The Flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALLUP into PULLA. 'The Flask' looks like a pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampulla is a small two-handled flask, as used for holy oil.

clue.text: Ray got exhausted and withdrew

parts.note: ray or re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A man named Ray became worn out and left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a name; it is the note RE (doh, ray, me).
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to withdraw from a place or activity.

clue.text: It's an advantage to be born healthy

parts.note: the verb be, taken from to be
NE is née, born, as in maiden names

explanation.surface: Coming into the world in good health gives a head start.
explanation.walkthrough: NE is a crossword form of née, French for born.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or advantage that something brings.

clue.text: Order heeded in the saleroom

definitions.meaning: a command obeyed, as in doing someone's will
making offers at an auction

explanation.surface: Instructions are followed at the auction house.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a command one carries out and also offers made at an auction.

clue.text: Airmen retreat into temple with a flourish

indicators.note: the turned word for airmen goes inside the word for temple

parts.note: fane is a poetic word for temple

indicators.note: the airmen go backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: Pilots withdraw into a shrine with ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns RAF to FAR; 'into' puts it in FANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a trumpet flourish announcing someone.

clue.text: Russian writer sadly lost fiddle

indicators.note: the word lost is sadly treated, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novelist laments a missing violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges LOST into TOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy, author of War and Peace, is a famous Russian novelist.

clue.text: A buccaneer in South Dakota sounded his aitches

indicators.note: the word for buccaneer sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota

explanation.surface: A pirate in the American Midwest speaks carefully, pronouncing every H.
explanation.walkthrough: SD is the US postal code for South Dakota; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirated sound is breathed, so saying an H properly is aspirating it.

clue.text: Some of the poor wretches may try to be sick

indicators.note: only some letters of the words are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A few of the unfortunate people may feel nauseous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' picks out the run in wRETCHes.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to make the motion of vomiting, attempting to throw up.

clue.text: Ford left record of the year's events

parts.note: Anna Ford, a well-known British television newsreader

explanation.surface: A car maker departed from its yearly report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like the carmaker, but it is Anna Ford, a BBC and ITN newsreader.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is the yearly entry in a chronicle recording that year's happenings.

clue.text: Telephone celebrity by satellite

explanation.surface: A famous person phones in via satellite link.
explanation.walkthrough: Telstar was the 1962 satellite that relayed the first live transatlantic TV pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was the pioneering communications satellite, a specific example of the category.

clue.text: One Pole to demand payment? That's not right

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to exact is to demand payment

explanation.surface: Someone from Poland pressing for money is in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person, but it is N, the north pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise or inaccurate, hence not correct.

clue.text: Attained by Communist without pain

indicators.note: the old sense outside: the word for Communist goes round the word for pain

explanation.surface: Achieved by a Communist with no suffering at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: a common crossword trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a goal is to attain it, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Cheap seats in the picture house

definitions.meaning: the highest, cheapest tier in a theatre
an art ... displaying paintings

explanation.surface: Inexpensive places to sit at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture house' suggests a cinema; here it is a building showing paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the top theatre balcony with cheap seats and a building for showing art.
